title: Jebel Irhoud
summary: A cave site in Morocco where miners found human fossils in the 1960s and later excavations led by Jean-Jacques Hublin recovered remains of at least five individuals. Dated to about 300,000 years ago, they are among the oldest securely dated Homo sapiens fossils and point to a pan-African origin of the species.

uncertainty.note: Opened sources give "around 300,000 years" with no error range; zeros mean not stated.

where.modern_name: Jbel Ighoud (Jebel Irhoud), Youssoufia Province, Marrakesh-Safi, Morocco
where.historical_name: No polity; Middle Stone Age site in what is now Morocco

importance.justification: Holds some of the oldest securely dated Homo sapiens fossils, pushing the species back about 100,000 years.
